title: Fisher's principle of equal investment in the sexes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fisher's principle of equal investment in the sexes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Under random mating and autosomal inheritance, selection drives parents to invest equally in sons and daughters, which gives a 1:1 sex ratio when the two cost the same.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: ESS allocation: N_m c_m = N_f c_f; with c_m = c_f the unbeatable primary sex ratio is 1:1

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection (1930)

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: Ronald A. Fisher (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: panmixia, autosomal control of the sex ratio, each offspring has one father and one mother, no local mate competition or sex-specific resource competition

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: proved as an invasion (ESS) result (Shaw and Mohler 1953). Its own named exceptions (local mate competition, Hamilton 1967) are predicted deviations, not refutations.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: ESS allocation: N_m c_m = N_f c_f; with c_m = c_f the unbeatable primary sex ratio is 1:1

fields.label: Proposed test
fields.value: Compare population sex-investment ratios (numbers times per-offspring cost) across species that meet the panmixia assumption, and test that experimentally perturbed sex ratios return toward equal investment.
